edges.target: Misfolded Protein Aggregation in Peripheral Neurons

edges.source: Misfolded Protein Aggregation in Peripheral Neurons

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint: an axonal sensorimotor neuropathy of adult onset and moderate severity, confirmed by nerve conduction studies and supported by sural nerve biopsy. Adult onset is itself characteristic — most CMT presents in the first two decades, while axonal subtypes increasingly present in adulthood, and BAG3 belongs to that later-onset group. Lower limb MRI shows a selective pattern, with fatty infiltration more severe in soleus and the deep posterior compartment than in medial gastrocnemius and the anterior compartment.

evidence.snippet: Bcl2-associated athanogene 3 (BAG3) is a multifunctional cochaperone responsible for protein quality control within cells.

nodes.description: Heterozygous variants affect the conserved IPV motif region of BAG3, the surface through which it binds the small heat shock protein HSPB8. The recurrent CMT2JJ allele is p.Pro209Ser (c.625C>T), reported in three families and then independently in a Chinese family, and proposed on that basis to be a hotspot with more than one ethnic origin. It sits at the same codon as the myofibrillar myopathy allele p.Pro209Leu (c.626C>T) — adjacent nucleotides, one codon, two diseases.

evidence.reference_title: BAG3 p.Pro209Ser mutation identified in a Chinese family with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Recently, a novel c.625C>T (p.Pro209Ser) mutation in BAG3 was reported to cause axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease in three families.

evidence.reference_title: BAG3 p.Pro209Ser mutation identified in a Chinese family with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: The p.Pro209Ser mutation with different ethnic origins might be another hotspot mutation of BAG3.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline missense variants at the IPV motif. The action is a toxic gain of function, not haploinsufficiency or a simple dominant negative: the Pro209 mutants as a class acquire a new property, relocating themselves and their chaperone partners into insoluble aggresomes. This was shown for all Pro209 mutants together, p.Pro209Ser included, rather than inferred from the myopathy allele alone.

nodes.description: BAG3 is the co-chaperone of chaperone-assisted selective autophagy: with HSPB8 and Hsp70 it transports misfolded proteins to the microtubule organizing center for degradation in autophagosomes. The Pro209 mutants do not merely fail at this — they actively subvert it, relocating CASA-complex chaperones into insoluble aggresomes and trapping ubiquitinylated client proteins there so they cannot be cleared. This was demonstrated for the Pro209 mutant class including p.Pro209Ser, which is why this node is ESTABLISHED rather than inferred from the myopathy allele.

evidence.reference_title: The role of BAG3 in dilated cardiomyopathy and its association with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2.
evidence.snippet: BAG3 interacts with chaperones HSPB8 and Hsp70 to transport misfolded proteins to the Microtubule Organizing Center (MTOC) and degrade them in autophagosomes in a process known as Chaperone Assisted Selective Autophagy (CASA).

evidence.reference_title: BAG3 Pro209 mutants associated with myopathy and neuropathy relocate chaperones of the CASA-complex to aggresomes.
evidence.snippet: We found that all BAG3_Pro209 mutants have acquired a toxic gain-of-function, which causes these variants to accumulate in the form of insoluble HDAC6- and vimentin-positive aggresomes.

evidence.reference_title: Myopathy associated BAG3 mutations lead to protein aggregation by stalling Hsp70 networks.
evidence.snippet: As a consequence, the mutant BAG3 proteins become the node for a dominant gain of function causing aggregation of itself, Hsp70, Hsp70 clients and tiered interactors within the BAG3 interactome.

nodes.description: Aggresome formation and client entrapment are directly demonstrated for the Pro209 mutants, so the aggregation itself is not in doubt. What remains PROVISIONAL is specifically the peripheral-neuron step: the aggresome work was done in cell lines, no study has shown aggregates in nerve tissue from a CMT2JJ patient, and the supporting argument that aggregation is what damages the axon leans additionally on the analogy with HSPB1 p.Pro182Leu in CMT2. A closer corroboration than that analogy is that HSPB8 — one of the small heat-shock proteins the Pro209 motif binds directly — itself causes axonal CMT2 when mutated, so the client side of this chaperone relationship is independently established as a peripheral-neuropathy mechanism. The gradual loss of protein homeostasis these mutants produce is the plausible route to axonal degeneration; it has not been observed in the affected tissue.
